Definition: from τρίβω (to "rub"; akin to τείρω, τρύω, and the base of G5131, G5134); a rut or worn track:--path.
BiblicalUsage: Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make His paths straight — the voice in the wilderness in Isaiah, in Mark and in Luke, the same word every time. Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make His paths straight — the voice in the wilderness in Isaiah, in Mark and in Luke, the same word every time.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the repetition is the point: the path is made straight by a voice, and the voice has been crying it since Isaiah.
